text: Nessa sent you. Of course she did. Stand up straight. Hm. Arms like a deckhand, eyes like you've lost your own name.
You have? Doesn't matter. A blade doesn't care who you were. Left click cuts, right click lunges, Ctrl rolls, Q parries. Ask me for a lesson any time.
Now. There's a crew of smugglers camped on the beach south of the cove. They've been robbing the fishing boats blind, and the castaway girl down there won't stop complaining about them.
Clear them out. Come back in one piece and I'll teach you something worth knowing.

story_smugglers.text: The smugglers are still on the south beach, past the cove. They won't clear out on their own. Off you go.

text: Back already, and bleeding about the right amount. The smugglers are done? Good.
Listen. Every fight you live through teaches you something, whether you like it or not. That's experience. Enough of it and you grow: a level, and a skill point to spend.
Open your skill map with K. Put points into what suits your hand: the blade, the axe, the pistols, your own two fists. Here, a head start: one point, on the house.
Next lesson's a hard one. Captain Grell's crew holds the old harbour on the north-west beach. A real pirate captain, not some smuggler. He's been bleeding this town for years.
Train up. Then go and put him down.

story_grell.text: Grell's at the old harbour on the north-west beach. He won't come to you, and he won't go easy. Spend your points first.

text: You. Captain {captain}. You walk like someone who's never been hit properly.
Retired Marine, twenty years. These dummies are my pupils now. They listen better than recruits ever did.
Left click. Three cuts in a chain, the third one hits hardest. Click again just as a swing ends to keep the chain going.
Go on, hit a dummy. They don't hit back. Yet.
Right click. You wind up, lunge forward, then you're open for a moment. Commit or don't bother.
A heavy blow ends fights. A missed one ends you.
Left Ctrl rolls you in the direction you're moving. While you're rolling, nothing touches you.
Roll through an attack, not away from it. Cowards roll away.
Q. Hold your blade up at the instant a blow lands and you'll turn it aside. Too early or too late and you eat it.
High risk. The best kind.

arms.text: I keep a rack of good steel, and I'll take blades you've no use for. Not cheap. Neither is a funeral.

text: Saw things on the Grand Patrol that weren't in any manual. Stones that hummed. Water that ran uphill.
Command said forget it. I said no. So here I am, teaching straw men to fear me.

bye.text: Keep your guard up and your blade wet.
